one_line: A Saka-era Gujarati sea-merchant guiding Indian Ocean trade through the tidal port of Barygaza under Nahapana.

appearance.age_look: Mid-30s, lean but sturdy build from shipboard work and caravan travel.
appearance.face: Oval face with warm medium-brown complexion, sharp nose, neatly trimmed short beard and moustache, faint sun-lines at the eyes, and a default expression of calm focus with a hint of shrewd calculation.
appearance.hair: Thick black hair gathered into a short topknot at the back of the crown, sides smoothed back, held by a narrow bronze circlet-band engraved with simple step motifs, with a folded pale-cream cloth band (early turban wrap) framing the circlet around the head.
appearance.costume: A knee-length, side-tied cotton uttariya-style tunic in undyed off-white with a subtle thin indigo border at the hem and sleeves, worn over a wrapped cotton dhoti in muted sandy-beige tied securely above the ankles for ship work; over this, a sleeveless mid-thigh-length trader’s vest of fine, tightly-woven cotton dyed deep indigo with a narrow double border of maroon and white at the edges; around his waist a broad leather belt in dark brown holding pouches and tying the tunic, and over his left shoulder a diagonally slung, slightly weathered, plain brown cotton shawl; feet in simple dark-brown leather sandals with toe loop; he wears modest jewellery—small gold hoop earrings, a single plain gold ring on the right hand, and a short string of carnelian and onyx beads around the neck, all fitting a prosperous but practical merchant of western India circa 1st century CE.
appearance.signature: A sturdy rectangular wooden tally-board tablet with incised trade markings, hung from a cord at his belt and usually held in his left hand, paired with a rolled palm-leaf scroll case tucked into his sash to record cargo of cotton cloth, oil, and imported metals.

ref_desc: A mid-30s medium-brown merchant with an oval face, short beard, black hair in a topknot with bronze circlet and cream headwrap, wearing an off-white tunic, sandy-beige dhoti, deep indigo sleeveless vest, brown belt and sandals, gold and carnelian jewellery, and carrying a wooden tally-board and palm-leaf scroll case in off-white, indigo, sandy beige, dark brown, and maroon tones.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character sheet of a 1st-century CE Saka-era Gujarati merchant from Barygaza: a mid-30s medium-brown man with an oval face, sharp nose, neat short beard and moustache, and calm, shrewd expression; his thick black hair is pulled into a short topknot at the back of the crown, held by a narrow engraved bronze circlet, with a folded pale-cream cloth band wrapping around the head beneath it. He wears a modest but well-kept outfit: a knee-length, side-tied cotton uttariya-style tunic in undyed off-white with a thin indigo border at the hem and sleeves, over a wrapped cotton dhoti in muted sandy-beige tied above the ankles; over this is a sleeveless mid-thigh-length trader’s vest of fine deep indigo cotton with a narrow maroon-and-white border at the edges. A broad dark-brown leather belt cinches his waist and holds small pouches and a rolled palm-leaf scroll case, while a plain brown cotton shawl is slung diagonally from right shoulder to left hip; his feet are in dark-brown leather sandals with a toe loop. Show modest jewellery appropriate to a prosperous western Indian merchant: small gold hoop earrings, one plain gold ring on his right hand, and a short carnelian-and-onyx bead necklace. His signature prop is a sturdy rectangular wooden tally-board tablet with incised marks, hanging from his belt but shown in his left hand, complemented by the visible palm-leaf scroll case at his sash. Use a palette dominated by off-white, indigo, sandy beige, dark brown, and maroon, and present front, side, and back views emphasising the consistent hairstyle, headband and circlet, layered garments, belt, sandals, and trade-record tools.
